repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for every changed shape: column classification/tags in ingestion.schema.discovered.v1 and metadata.dataset.changed.v1, the metadata-service column API and new classification endpoint, masked_columns on the entitlements Decision and on the query response; released as minor 2.4.0.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Its explicit dataclasses drop undeclared fields, so Column.classification/tags and Decision.masked_columns must be added (plus a set-classification client method and the platform-contracts 2.4.0 pin) or no service will ever see the new data; released as 3.5.0.

repositories.name: metadata-service
repositories.reason: Owning service: store classification/source/tags per column, suggest classification from ingested tags, keep steward overrides across re-discovery, add the steward override endpoint, and return classification in GET columns and in metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: The Postgres connector already reads column_comment (e.g. 'tags: pii,email') but drops it; it must parse the tags and publish them on each column of ingestion.schema.discovered.v1.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Access decisions must return masked_columns (columns classified PII when the principal lacks a pii:read grant), which needs column classifications from metadata-service and column-aware cache invalidation.

repositories.name: consumption-gateway
repositories.reason: Entitlements only decides and enforcement happens in the caller, so the gateway must mask the masked_columns in returned rows (behind a rollout flag) and upgrade to platform-sdk 3.5.0 so Decision keeps masked_columns.

repositories.name: transformation-service
repositories.reason: Rules are currently bound only by data_type; PII-format validation rules must be added and bound to columns whose classification is PII (read via platform-sdk 3.5.0 get_columns).

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: It validates metadata.dataset.changed.v1 against a strict vendored 2.1.0 schema (additionalProperties: false on columns), so the additive classification field would dead-letter every event unless the vendored schema is updated and deployed first.

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: Cross-service suites must be extended (tags to classification, steward override, masked query results, PII transformation rules) and existing suites re-run to prove no breaking change.

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Consumes the modified metadata.dataset.changed.v1 but is a tolerant reader of only dataset.urn and dataset.name, so it needs a consumer contract test against a 2.4.0 sample payload, not a code change.

repositories.name: reporting-service
repositories.reason: Listed by metadata-service as a consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1 but its repository is not in the workspace, so its tolerance of the new column fields must be confirmed with its owners.

considered_not_impacted.name: notification-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Uses only dataset_urn and score from transformation.result.published.v1 (unchanged schema) and Dataset.owner from get_dataset (unchanged); PII rules may lower scores and trigger more owner emails, which is intended behaviour.

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes consumption.access.logged.v1 (principal, dataset_urn, row_count), which this plan does not change; masking does not change row counts.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lower-case strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. ["pii","email"]); no new required fields.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional, nullable columns[].classification (PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII), columns[].classification_source (SUGGESTED|STEWARD) and columns[].tags; classification changes are published with the existing COLUMNS_CHANGED change_type (no new enum value). Additive per platform-contracts semver, but it breaks search-indexer's strict vendored schema until that is updated.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Each Column gains optional nullable classification, classification_source and tags fields (null when unclassified).

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: Steward sets or overrides a column classification (body {classification}); stores classification_source=STEWARD, returns the updated Column, publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 COLUMNS_CHANGED; 400 on invalid value, 403 without steward permission, 404 on unknown dataset/column.

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decide
contracts.description: Decision response gains masked_columns (array of column names classified PII that must be masked because the principal lacks pii:read; empty when nothing to mask or when allow=false); request unchanged.

contracts.name: POST /v1/query
contracts.description: Values of masked columns in rows are replaced by a mask (row keys and row count unchanged), and the 200 response gains optional masked_columns listing which columns were masked.

open_questions: Masking format: fixed string token (e.g. "****") for strings and null for non-strings, or type-preserving/partial masking (e.g. keep email domain)? Null may break consumers that assume NOT NULL columns.
Is pii:read a single global grant, or should it also be scoped (pii:domain:<domain>:read, pii:dataset:<urn>:read) like the existing read grants?
Which service principals (BI tools, pipelines) legitimately need unmasked PII and must be granted pii:read before enforcement is switched on?

How does consumption-gateway map result columns to dataset columns for arbitrary SQL (aliases, expressions, joins across datasets)? Name matching alone can be bypassed with 'SELECT email AS e'; should such queries be rejected or masked fail-closed, or should masking move to the warehouse (masking views/policies)?
Who is a steward and how is the PUT classification endpoint authorized (new entitlements grant such as metadata:classify, or dataset owner)? Is an audit trail of overrides required?

Tag vocabulary for suggestions: which comment tags map to PII, CONFIDENTIAL, INTERNAL, PUBLIC, and what is the precedence when several are present? Assumed: any of pii/email/phone/ssn -> PII, else confidential -> CONFIDENTIAL, internal -> INTERNAL, public -> PUBLIC, otherwise null.
Should unclassified (null) columns stay unmasked (assumed) or be treated fail-closed?
Backfill: existing datasets have no tags until their schema is re-discovered; do we trigger a full re-discovery, a one-off backfill job, or rely on steward classification?

Which PII-format rules are required (email, phone E.164, national id, ...) and are they chosen by the column's tags (e.g. 'email') or by explicit rule bindings via /v1/rules? Columns classified PII by a steward with no subtype tag need a default rule.
Should PII-format rule failures affect the dataset quality score (and therefore owner emails from notification-service), or be reported separately?
Should consumption.access.logged.v1 record masked_columns for audit? Not included here to keep usage-metering untouched.
Only the Postgres connector is in the workspace; do other ingestion connectors exist that also need tag extraction?

reporting-service is listed as a metadata.dataset.changed.v1 consumer in the metadata-service README but is not in the workspace, and the README omits search-indexer and lineage-service; who owns reporting-service, and is it a strict or tolerant reader?
Should search-indexer index classification (e.g. allow searching for PII columns) or just accept and ignore it? This plan only requires accepting it.
